item.text: {"case_id":"SPR00362","decision":"candidate","candidate_ranking":["C01","C23","C22"],"selected_candidate_label":"C01","confidence":0.99,"relationship_type":"both","rationale":"C01 materially supplied the child’s drafting. The child reproduces C01’s detailed Annecy Protocol authority recital nearly verbatim, expressly identifies C01 as the May 13, 1950 proclamation being supplemented, and builds its butter-quota provision directly upon the rate and quota that C01 activated. C23 is also a strong template for the child’s agreement-termination machinery, while C22 is an earlier close model for prorating a butter tariff quota that became effective partway through its quota period. C01 ranks first because its provisions are directly incorporated into, and then adjusted by, the child.","shared_material":[{"child_excerpt":"pursuant to the authority vested in the President by the Constitution and the statutes, including section 350 of the Tariff Act of 1930 ... on October 10, 1949, I entered into a trade agreement providing for the accession to the General Agreement on Tariffs and Trade ... which trade agreement for accession consists of the Annecy Protocol of Terms of Accession","parent_excerpt":"pursuant to the authority vested in the President by the Constitution and the statutes, including section 350 of the Tariff Act of 1930 ... on October 10, 1949, I entered into a trade agreement providing for the accession to the General Agreement on Tariffs and Trade ... which trade agreement for accession consists of the Annecy Protocol of Terms of Accession","explanation":"The child closely reproduces C01’s lengthy and distinctive description of the statutory authority, participating governments, and Annecy Protocol."},{"child_excerpt":"the said Proclamation of May 13, 1950, made effective, on and after May 28, 1950, the rate of duty of 7 cents per pound specified in item 709 ... with respect to not more than 5,000,000 pounds of butter","parent_excerpt":"the identification of each of the concessions provided for in Part I of the said Schedule XX in Annex A which is included in the eighth recital ... shall ... be included in the list set forth in the ninth recital of the said proclamation of December 22, 1949","explanation":"C01 is the May 13 proclamation that activated the Schedule XX concessions on specified accession dates; the child expressly supplements that action and adjusts the resulting butter quota."},{"child_excerpt":"the said tariff quota ... became effective in the second month of the period ... and I determine that it would be appropriate ... to limit the quantity of butter dutiable at the rate of 7 cents per pound ... during the remainder of the said quota period","parent_excerpt":"To the end that the said trade agreement for accession ... may be carried out, the identification of each of the concessions ... shall, on and after the date set forth ... be included in the list","explanation":"The child uses C01’s concession-activation framework as the predicate for a tailored mid-period quota adjustment, preserving the same administrative machinery while adding the prorated quantity."}]}
